name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Audit the prompt inventory first. A routing system can’t improve what it doesn’t measure—current prompts may be stale, redundant, or misaligned with actual use. The trade-off is time spent cataloging instead of tweaking, but without this baseline we risk optimizing the wrong parts. Once we know which prompts drive 80% of traffic, we can target routing and engine changes precisely.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t stale prompts—it’s that auditing assumes we know what “good” looks like. Without a decision on *how* we’ll measure prompt quality (e.g., user success rates, latency impact, or error reduction), the inventory is just noise. Settle it by defining the metric first, then audit against that.
